questions.prompt: What is the core move in this strategy?
choices: Appear compliant while quietly building leverage underneath
Challenge the stronger side as early as possible
Avoid every form of hidden preparation

explanation.gentle: The chapter defines the strategy through hidden construction under a surface of compliance.
explanation.direct: Start with the mechanism: outward submission covers covert capacity building until open contest is survivable.
explanation.competitive: The play is to grow force under the mask instead of dying in an early frontal fight.

questions.prompt: Why can direct defiance fail for a weaker operator?
choices: It is always morally superior
The stronger side may control punishment, timing, and visibility
It automatically builds quiet leverage

explanation.gentle: The problem is power asymmetry, not just lack of courage.
explanation.direct: Notice the trap: the stronger side can force the conflict to happen before the weaker side has real options.
explanation.competitive: The big side wants the fight early because early is when it can kill it cleanly.

questions.prompt: Where does the chapter place the ethical line?
choices: At any hidden preparation at all
Only at open sabotage
When covert leverage replaces honest disagreement or exit that was actually available

explanation.gentle: The line appears when necessity disappears and bad faith remains.
explanation.direct: Mark the boundary here: concealment becomes corrosive when clean disagreement or fair exit was genuinely possible.
explanation.competitive: The dirty turn begins when the mask is chosen for convenience instead of survival.

questions.prompt: Kestrel is trapped under a manager who punishes visible challenge. What is the strongest adjustment?
choices: Stage a public confrontation before more time is lost
Build quiet allies, competence, and options before any visible clash
Withdraw from all leverage-building to avoid looking strategic

explanation.gentle: He needs survivable leverage, not faster conflict.
explanation.direct: Change the timing: grow real capacity first because open challenge now would be crushed too early.
explanation.competitive: Refuse the kill window and build underneath it.

questions.prompt: Noor hears praise for covert undermining in general. What should she test first?
choices: Whether the operator is the weaker party
Whether direct challenge or fair process was actually blocked
Whether the tactic looks subtle enough to work

explanation.gentle: She is testing necessity, not elegance.
explanation.direct: Check the channel conditions: if honest disagreement or exit was available, the covert move is much harder to defend.
explanation.competitive: Ask whether the mask was forced by coercion or chosen because it was easier.

questions.prompt: Harlan is under a retaliatory director. What is the best immediate move?
choices: Publicly expose the director at once
Quietly build leverage that reduces dependence before forcing any open contest
Accept the hierarchy permanently and stop preparing

explanation.gentle: He needs a stronger base before visible resistance.
explanation.direct: Grow allies, competence, and options first so the later contest is not one-sided from the start.
explanation.competitive: Build the force first and stop offering the strong side an easy execution.

questions.prompt: Tovah could use hidden leverage in a non-coercive relationship. Which response fits the chapter?
choices: Use concealment because it avoids discomfort
Choose direct conversation or exit because the context does not justify the mask
Build a parallel campaign slowly so the other person never sees it

explanation.gentle: The framework has context limits, not just tactical rules.
explanation.direct: This is a misuse case: where good-faith conflict is possible, covert undermining becomes bad faith.
explanation.competitive: Do not go underground when the room can still hold a clean fight.

questions.prompt: Orin is considering a hidden parallel structure under a dominant senior member. What is the strongest test?
choices: Whether the formal route is truly blocked and the hidden build restores agency instead of serving revenge
Whether the senior member is unpopular
Whether secrecy can be maintained indefinitely

explanation.gentle: The question is whether the hidden build is necessary and disciplined.
explanation.direct: Use the blocked-channel and endpoint test: confirm coercion first, then keep the covert build tied to restored agency rather than payback.
explanation.competitive: Make sure the blind-spot build is a shield, not a vendetta.

questions.prompt: When is this strategy most legitimate?
choices: When blocked channels or coercive dominance make direct challenge unsafely premature
When covert action feels more comfortable than honest disagreement
When the operator wants maximum surprise even in a fair setting

explanation.gentle: Legitimacy here depends on necessity under asymmetry.
explanation.direct: The narrow clean version requires real coercion or blocked channels that make open challenge nonviable too early.
explanation.competitive: A forced mask can be strategy. A convenient mask is just duplicity.
